My answers will sound weird but whatever.

The first game I ever played that had characters I truly cared about was the original XCOM back in 1994. Yeah, they're randomly generated grunts, but it was the first game I ever played that let me name all those grunts and let me project on to them a personality and background. And it was the first game that really made me feel something when they died, not necessarily because their loss meant much mechanically (unlike the remake your soldiers did not become godlike superwarriors after a couple of missions) but because we'd shared so much time, so much struggle. I loved my heroes more than I've loved any others in anything. RIP 'Frog' Johanneson, I'll nevar forgit.

Trying to think of an established franchise that I care about, I guess the characters from Ocarina of Time were kinda 'lovable,' but I think that is more about projection than their actual behavior. Much of OoT is archetypal, and Link's struggle is touchingly heroic but I don't know that I'd call him, or any of the other characters, particularly lovable.

I know I'm forgetting something important but I think the game that had the most 'lovable' characters, for me, was Halflife 2. Halflife 1 was one of the most important gaming experiences of my life, not to mention how important it was to gaming. Its realistic environments, clever AI, and scripted events (wow, remember when those were new?) changed the expectations for the entire industry. There were no characters to speak of, not really, just the player as Gordon Freeman. The sequel, however, managed to gloss over this and succeeded at retconning in Barney the security guard (yeah I know he's from Blue Shift, whatever), Issac Kleiner, and Eli Vance as Gordon's friends and associates, and adding Alyx and D0g.

After the profound experience I had with HL1, introducing all these characters (Barney and the scientists being something of a distillation of numerous similar characters from the first game into a singular personality and person) as meaningful pieces of the plot warmed my heart, and of course it helped that everyone wanted to tell me how great I was.

HL2 is nearly 10 years old now and is no longer graphically 'impressive' but when it released the expressiveness of the models alone was amazing and even today they're pretty good; this helped lend unexpected humanity to the characters and make them memorable and sympathetic. D0g's animation did the same thing. Most powerful of all, I suppose, was the way the characters reacted believably to the character and each other, cared about each other in the dystopian wasteland of City 17, and worked towards ending the tyranny of the Combine. The quality of the voice acting (and the return of several actors) played no small part in the characters' believability as well.

It is the actions they take, on top of all this, that makes them lovable to me: Isaac Kleiner and his defanged headcrab, Barney joking about that beer he owes you, Eli's love and concern for Alyx (and vice versa), D0g and Alyx's behavior in general. Even Grigori is kind of lovable, the crazy bastard. and the Vorlons, and your little antlion army. Hell, even the condescending authoritarianism of Dr. Breen is kind of lovable in a certain way.

So if I had to choose the game that had the MOST (as in most numerous) lovable characters I'd go with HL2.

But a number of games and respective characters deserve an honorable mention: Minsc from Baldur's Gate 1 and 2 (and Boo, of course); Wheatley from Portal 2; the entire cast of Sly Cooper; most of the cast of Okami. I'm sure there's many more but my brain isn't working.
